audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove was written as an 'E pull' to sidestep with no mention that only the returning wave roots, Vision of Empire's enormous cast range was never stated, and Demonic Ascension was described as if it had a fixed duration.
audit.why: These three are the whole matchup for a 950-range enchanter: dodge the return not the throw; expect a W dropped from off-screen; and his R ends itself the moment you stop being a drain target.
audit.corrected: All three written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5] and mid, with the 12s Nevermove cooldown and the 5500+ W range.

edits.before: This is your bullying peak. Multiple Q and RQ Soulflare rotations push him off the wave and let you tax plates behind Inspire's speed — he has zero dash to punish your step-up. Keep dodging the E pull; as long as it whiffs he can't set up the W zone or chain into his drain. At 6 his R Demonic Ascension is the one button that flips an extended fight, so bait it, RW-heal or E-shield the burst, and leave — never stand and brawl inside his draining AoE.
edits.after: This is your bullying peak. Multiple Q and RQ Soulflare rotations push him off the wave and let you tax plates behind Inspire's speed — he has zero dash to punish your step-up. Keep dodging Nevermove; only its returning wave roots, and while it whiffs he has no setup at all. Watch for a Vision of Empire dropped from off-screen — its cast range runs past 5500 units. At 6, bait Demonic Ascension, RW-heal or E-shield the burst, and leave: it only lasts while he drains a champion.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. It governs your forward steps. - E shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, and only the returning wave roots — sidestep on the way back, not the way out. It also returns faster while his R is up. - Demonic Ascension lasts only as long as he drains a champion: walk out and it ends itself.

edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return, not the throw. Demonic Ascension only persists while he drains a champion — leave and it drops him.

notes: Chart on disk was inverted against both the packet and its own whys on six of seven rows. The three real interactions the page lacked: Nevermove roots only on the return sweep, Vision of Empire can be cast from 5500+ units away (so it arrives from fog), and Demonic Ascension self-terminates when no champion is being drained. Row 6 is the one place I took the packet over the existing why, which read as a clean Swain scaling win; I reworded the why to an even read rather than leave the two disagreeing. No mirror existed for this matchup yet.
